nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a monoid homomorphism. Then there is a simple finite-dimensional complex representation $V$ of $G$ whose character equals $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Every homomorphism of a finite abelian group to the complex numbers is a simple character

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $V$ be a simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$. Then there is a monoid homomorphism $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ such that the character of $V$ equals $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Characters of simple representations of a finite abelian group are homomorphisms

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $V$ and $W$ be simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with characters $\chi_V$ and $\chi_W$. If $\chi_V = \chi_W$, then $V$ and $W$ are isomorphic.
nodes.title: Characters determine simple representations of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. The character $\chi_V : G \to k$ of $V$, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace of the action of $g$ on $V$, satisfies $\chi_V(1) = 1$ and $\chi_V(gh) = \chi_V(g)\,\chi_V(h)$ for all…
nodes.title: The character of a simple representation as a monoid homomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. Let $\chi_V : G \to k$ be the character of $V$, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace of the action of $g$ on $V$. Then $\chi_V(gh) = \chi_V(g)\,\chi_V(h)$ for all $g, h \in G$.
nodes.title: Characters of simple representations of commutative monoids are multiplicative

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. The character of $V$, regarded as a monoid homomorphism from $G$ to $k$, has the character $\chi_V : G \to k$ of $V$ as its underlying function, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace…
nodes.title: The character homomorphism has the character as its underlying function

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $G$ be a commutative monoid. Every finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$ has dimension $1$ over $k$.
nodes.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations of commutative monoids are one-dimensional

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a monoid. If a finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$ is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$, then $V$ is irreducible as a representation: $V \ne 0$, and the only subrepresentations of $V$ are $0$ and $V$.
nodes.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations of a monoid are irreducible

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ defined by $\varphi$. For every $g \in G$, the action of $g$ on $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi(g)$ times the identity map of $k$.
nodes.title: The action in the one-dimensional representation of a homomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. The character of $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi$: the trace of the action of each $g \in G$ on $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi(g)$.
nodes.title: The character of the representation of a homomorphism is the homomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. Then $k_\varphi$ has dimension $1$ over $k$.
nodes.title: The representation of a homomorphism is one-dimensional

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. Then $k_\varphi$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$.
nodes.title: The representation of a homomorphism is simple

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, and let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism. This is the finite-dimensional representation $k_\varphi$ of $G$ on the one-dimensional space $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$, that is, by the linear map $x \mapsto \varphi(g)\,x$.
nodes.title: The one-dimensional representation of a homomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $G$ a monoid with commutative multiplication, and $V$ a simple finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ (a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional representations), with action $\rho$ and character $\chi_V(g) = \operatorname{tr} \rho(g)$. nodes.title: Simple representations of commutative monoids act by scalars

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
